name: F5 WAF — Targeted Web-Attack Campaign Against Internet Banking
description:
Attacker objective
Compromise internet-banking applications by probing them with a broad exploitation toolkit (SQLi, XSS, command execution, code injection, traversal, RFI, request smuggling, WAF evasion).

Attack logic
A legitimate client triggers at most one or two WAF attack categories incidentally. A single source that triggers several distinct dangerous categories within a short window is running an automated or targeted web-attack toolkit against the bank.

Why this detection works
Counting distinct dangerous attack types per source separates toolkit/campaign behaviour from incidental single-category hits.

False positives
Authorised vulnerability scanners / pentests; aggressive DAST from a partner.

Tuning
Raise the distinct-type threshold or shorten the window if noisy; allowlist sanctioned scanner IPs.

Required telemetry
F5 ASM / Advanced WAF events (CEF): attack_type, source.ip, policy/app, deviceAction.
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. source.ip = the attacker; review the distinct attack types and whether any were not blocked (reached the app).
2. Correlate with the targeted policy/app and block the source if hostile.
false_positives: Authorised vulnerability scanners / pentests; aggressive DAST from a partner.
query: observer.vendor:"F5" and cef.extensions.deviceCustomString4:("SQL-Injection" or "Cross Site Scripting (XSS)" or "Command Execution" or "Server Side Code Injection" or "Path Traversal" or "Remote File Include" or "HTTP Request Smuggling Attack" or "Session Hijacking" or "Detection Evasion" or "Trojan/Backdoor/Spyware" or "JSON Parser Attack" or "Injection Attempt")
